requirements:
Integer polygon geometry, level 1. All clauses below are normative.

R1. Implement in Rust as a SINGLE source file that compiles with `rustc --edition 2024`, std only. Output ONLY the Rust source code inside ```rust fences. Do not use inner attributes (`#![...]`) or inner documentation (`//!`).

R2. Expose exactly the public API listed below. Public data types must derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq; Point, Orientation, Location (when present), and Collinear (when present) must also derive Copy. Point ordering for all rules is lexicographic (x, then y); deriving Ord is optional. Fields and functions shown are public.

R3. Coordinates are i64 but accepted values lie in the inclusive interval [-1_000_000_000, 1_000_000_000]. Arithmetic and comparisons must be exact; no overflow or floating-point tolerance is allowed.

R4. A raw polygon input may contain at most 4096 vertices. Polygon preparation first checks raw length and returns TooManyVertices { len: raw_length } if exceeded, before examining coordinates.

R5. Next scan all raw polygon vertices in input order, including any closing vertex, and return OutOfRange { index } for the first invalid coordinate. This precedes minimum-length and all geometric checks.

R6. After these checks only, if raw length >= 2 and last point equals first point, remove exactly ONE last point. Do not repeatedly strip closure copies, merge adjacent equal points, or reorder vertices. Call the remaining slice the effective polygon.

R7. An effective polygon must contain at least 3 vertices, else return TooFewVertices { len: effective_length }. Empty input has effective length 0; one point has length 1; two equal points reduce to length 1.

R8. For an effective polygon of n points, edge i runs from vertex i to vertex (i+1) modulo n, including closing edge n-1. All indices returned for polygons refer to this original effective ordering unless canonical output is explicitly requested.

R9. measure(points) prepares the polygon and returns Measures. It allows zero-length edges, repeated vertices, collinearity, concavity, and self-intersection; it does not call validate, even at levels where validate exists.

R10. Measures.signed_area2 is the signed shoelace sum sum(x_i*y_next-y_i*x_next), in i128. Measures.area2 is its absolute value in u128, NOT the sum of absolute cross products; cancellation is intentional.

R11. Orientation is CounterClockwise for positive signed_area2, Clockwise for negative, and Degenerate for zero, regardless of self-intersection.

R12. For each edge with squared Euclidean distance d2, edge_milli[i] is the nearest integer to sqrt(d2 * 1_000_000), with exact half ties rounded upward. Zero-length edges produce 0. Round each edge separately.

R13. perimeter_milli is the u64 sum of the already rounded edge_milli values; never round the total unrounded perimeter. The closed polygon always includes all n edge lengths.

R14. longest_edge is Some(index) of the largest ROUNDED edge_milli, not the largest exact length. For tied rounded lengths, sort each edge's two endpoints lexicographically and choose the smallest resulting (low_endpoint, high_endpoint) pair; if still tied choose smallest edge index.

R15. Translation does not change area or lengths; reversing winding negates signed_area2 but keeps area2 and perimeter_milli. Edge indices and lengths must still follow the actual effective input order.

R16. All functions are deterministic, leave their input unchanged, and use the declared Result error variants. Return the first applicable error under the specified precedence; do not panic for any input satisfying the types, including i64::MIN and i64::MAX coordinates.

Exact public API (function declarations below describe signatures; provide their implementations):
```rust

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct Point { pub x: i64, pub y: i64 }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Orientation { Clockwise, Degenerate, CounterClockwise }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Measures {
    pub signed_area2: i128, pub area2: u128, pub orientation: Orientation,
    pub edge_milli: Vec<u64>, pub perimeter_milli: u64,
    pub longest_edge: Option<usize>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GeomError {
    TooManyVertices { len: usize },
    OutOfRange { index: usize },
    TooFewVertices { len: usize },
}

pub fn measure(points: &[Point]) -> Result<Measures, GeomError>;
```
